questions.q: Which register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.why: The program counter (PC) holds the address of the next instruction and is incremented during the fetch stage.

questions.q: What is the role of the control unit?
options: It stores data when the power is off
It performs arithmetic and logic calculations
It decodes instructions and coordinates the other components
It holds recently used data close to the CPU
questions.why: The control unit decodes instructions and sends control signals. Calculations are done by the ALU; cache holds frequently used data.

questions.q: Which of these is an embedded system?
options: A games console that runs many different games
The controller inside a washing machine
questions.why: An embedded system is built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function, such as a washing machine controller.

questions.q: Explain why a CPU with a larger cache can perform better than a CPU with a smaller cache.
questions.model: Cache is very fast memory close to the CPU that stores frequently used instructions and data. A larger cache can hold more of them, so the CPU has to fetch from the slower RAM less often and spends less time waiting.
points: cache stores frequently used data/instructions close to the CPU
larger cache means fewer slower accesses to RAM, so faster processing
